num is static, starts at 7, and r() returns num and then decrements it.
- init: r() [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 7 (num = 6)
- condition: r() [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 6, true; body prints r() [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 5
- update: r() [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 4; condition: r() [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 3, true; body prints r() [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2
- update: r() [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1; condition: r() [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0, false [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] stop

Output: 5 2

Answer: 52

For positive n, n/2 keeps getting smaller until it becomes 0. But the base case is n [latex]\lt[/latex] 0, which never happens: convert(0) calls convert(0) again forever.

printf comes after the recursive call, so nothing is ever printed. The program does not terminate (until the stack overflows).

Answer: It will not print anything and will not terminate
